title: SIPP care and work constraints differ by housing tenure
source_unit: SIPP person record by reference month, stratified by tenure, using final person and Fay-BRR replicate weights

observations.period: 2024 reference year; owned or being bought

denominator.unit: positive-final-person-weight selected person-record/month rows; each measure has its own tenure and conditional universe

observations.method: Official tenure, child-care status flags, and conditional universes; WPFINWGT full estimate and 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights with G=240 and perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: Intervals are design-based approximations; time lost is conditional on work prevention and remains imprecise.
observations.subgroup: ETENURE code 1: owned or being bought.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher paid-care use among owners/buyers may reflect resources, work, family composition, or care arrangements; tenure does not establish control over schedule or care access.

denominator.unit: positive-final-person-weight selected person-record/month rows; each measure has its own tenure and conditional universe

observations.method: Same official-universe and Fay-BRR method as the owner/buyer subgroup.
observations.uncertainty: Intervals are design-based approximations; time lost is conditional and less precise.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher work prevention among renters is compatible with housing and resource constraints but does not identify a housing cause, provider shortage, or employer response.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; occupied without payment of rent

denominator.unit: positive-final-person-weight selected person-record/month rows; each measure has its own tenure and conditional universe

reported_time_lost_from_work_due_to_chil.unit: not estimated: no valid records after the conditional work-prevention universe

observations.method: Same official-universe and Fay-BRR method; no time-lost estimate is promoted when all valid conditional records are absent.
observations.uncertainty: The subgroup is sparse and the available measures are imprecise; zero is an observed weighted estimate, not proof of no underlying cases.
observations.subgroup: ETENURE code 3: occupied without payment of rent.
observations.counterinterpretation: This small subgroup cannot support a reliable ranking against owners/buyers or renters.

related_sources.claim: Official tenure, child-care field labels, status flags, and universes.

boundary: This is a person-weighted, design-based tenure comparison. It does not establish household prevalence, housing causation, care access, schedule control, time substitution, recovery, trust, or political action.
